t:
That control and  jurisdiction over the following-described lands now comprising a portion  of the Acadia National Park, in the State of Maine, are hereby transferred from the Department of the Interior to the Department of the Navy:  Provided,  That the Secretary of the Interior shall retain  the right to approve the design of the buildings and structures to be placed thereon.
All that certain tract or parcel of land on Big Moose Island, Winter Harbor, Maine, which is bounded southerly and easterly by a chain link security fence, and northerly and westerly by the waters of Pond Island Cove and Frenchman Bay, and which is more particularly described as beginning at a point on the shore at the high-water mark of Frenchman Bay on the southwesterly side of Big Moose Island, so called, thence following the chain link security fence as now erected by the three, following courses and distances: North no degrees live minutes west one hundred and fifty-three feet; thence north thirty degrees twenty-four minutes east one hundred and fifty-seven and seven-tenths feet; thence south eighty-nine degrees nine minutes east one thousand four hundred and fifty-five and three-tenths feet to a point and angle in the said security fence which bears north thirty- four degrees fifty-four minutes west and is fifty feet distant at right angles from a point in the center line of the National Park Service road known as the Big Moose Island Road; thence turning to the left and following the said security fence in a general northerly direction but everywhere parallel with and fifty feet distant from the center line of the said Big Moose Island Road three thousand five hundred feet more or less to the high-water mark on the shore of Pond Island Cove; thence in a generally westerly and southerly direction but everywhere following the high-water mark of Pond Island Cove and Frenchman Bay seven thousand four hundred and seventy feet more or less to the place of beginning; except that portion thereof, containing twenty-five and ninety-six one-hundredths acres, which was transferred to the jurisdiction of the Department of the Navy pursuant to the Act of August 24, 1935 (ch. 644, 49 Stat. 795); the lands herein described containing one hundred and fifty-one and eighty-six one-hundredths acres after excluding the excepted portion.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Secretary of the Interior's retained right to approve building designs is a form of consultation or coordination. But that approval right runs between two federal departments (Interior and Navy), which is intra-government coordination. The section otherwise only transfers jurisdiction over described land and involves no state, local, public, or other outside party in any federal decision.
fable.s: Provided,  That the Secretary of the Interior shall retain  the right to approve the design of the buildings and structures to be placed thereon.

qwen_block.w: This section describes a transfer of jurisdiction between two federal agencies (Department of the Interior and Department of the Navy). The condition that the Secretary of the Interior retains approval rights over building designs is an internal check within the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: That control and jurisdiction over the following-described lands now comprising a portion of the Acadia National Park, in the State of Maine, are hereby transferred from the Department of the Interior to the Department of the Navy: Provided, That the Secretary of the Interior shall retain the right to approve the design of the buildings and structures to be placed thereon.

opus.w: The section moves control of land from one federal department to another. The only check on the Navy's decision is the Secretary of the Interior's approval of building designs. Because that approval stays entirely inside the federal government, it is coordination between agencies, not participation by an outside party. The rest of the section is a description of the land's boundaries.
opus.s: are hereby transferred from the Department of the Interior to the Department of the Navy:  Provided,  That the Secretary of the Interior shall retain  the right to approve the design of the buildings and structures to be placed thereon.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the proviso lets someone outside the Navy, the Secretary of the Interior, approve the design of the buildings before the Navy builds. That fails the definition: the Secretary of the Interior is a federal official. The land transfer and the design approval both happen between the Department of the Interior and the Department of the Navy. No state, tribe, expert or member of the public is involved.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Interior (a federal official) to approve designs for buildings on land transferred to the Department of the Navy (a federal agency). This is coordination between two entities within the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes consultation or coordination between federal agencies or officials from the definition of participation. Therefore, no outside party is involved in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That the Secretary of the Interior shall retain the right to approve the design of the buildings and structures to be placed thereon.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary of the Interior "approving the design" constitutes participation because it involves a federal official reviewing a proposal. However, the Secretary of the Interior is a federal official, and the Department of the Navy is a federal agency. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is **not** participation. Since both parties involved in the approval process are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not public participation.
